def normalize(text):
    text = tprep.normalize.hyphenated_words(text)
    text = tprep.normalize.quotation_marks(text)
    text = tprep.normalize.unicode(text)
    text = tprep.remove.accents(text)
    text = tprep.replace.phone_numbers(text)
    text = re.sub(r'http\S+', '', text) ##changed to this because tprep.replace did not work
    text = tprep.replace.emails(text)
    text = tprep.replace.user_handles(text)
    text = tprep.replace.emojis(text)
    text = text.lower()
    text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', text).encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    text = re.sub(r'<[^<>]*>', ' ', text)
    return text

topic_model_unpop.visualize_topics()

Interpret the results thoroughly (What labels would you give to the topics? What are the similarities or differences between the two models? What insights can you draw? What practical applications could this have?).

Note: unfortunately, there are a lot of cusswords. I did not predict that seeing as I thought I previewed the document carefully, but I also have no idea how to omit them from the data.

However, with tweets and mental health issues also accompany such things as cusswords, therefore, for now, I shall include it in my interpretation.

  • What labels would you give to the topics?

    • "Popular": "Positive" "Strength" and "Negative"
    • "Unpopular": "Negative", "Positve", and "Random"
    • I gave the negative label because some of the topics centered around pain, addiction, cuss words, and depression.
    • Positive because of reactions like "yass" which is a modern reaction to things in a good way. The strength label could also go for positve because it seems like the users are overcoming addictions, surving diseases and situations that affect mental health.

  • What are the similarities or differences between the two models?

    • similarities: Seeing as this data is centered around mental health, I do see some overlapping topics (e.g, addiction, foods, drinks, and strenght). Therefore similarities in the topics that are positve, and also those that are negative, Because both subsets highlight topics of depression, anxiety, and troubled mental health; plus, cusswords. While also, highlighting topics which show that users are seeing a positive side and experiencing positives such as healing, overcoming depreesion and/or addictions, or even surving cancer.

    • differences: frequency of cusswords appearing in both subsets under the topics differ.

  • What insights can you draw?

    • All in all, the topics for both subsets (popular and unpopular) show many similarities as it higlights topics that may directly relate to mental health of the user. Many users talked about overcoming depression, while many talked about going into depression- this is also accompanied with many other situations such as lifestyle, physical health, and environments. The topics and sentiments under mental health are quite similar in both subsets.

    • Also, there were recurring topics such as depression, anxiety, pain, food, exercise, anger

    • I would add that the popular subset probably had more positive topics and sentiments. This makes sense as more people would like to see "good" things. I might also argue that many people can relate or the people who posted had many more followers, therefore more outreach.

  • What practical applications could this have?

    • Due to NLP, I would say sentiment analysis to guage how people percieve mental health issues online and see which topics occur more, so it could highlight which areas are needed to be addressed. That is if we are planning to enhance mental health knowledge in hopes of helping people overcome difficulties and giving support to all who are healing.
